title: Abimelech Rules at Shechem (3 years)
summary: After Gideon's death his son Abimelech kills his seventy brothers, is made king at Shechem and reigns three years until he is killed at Thebez (Judg 9).
description: Judges-period record added from James B. Jordan's chronology (secondary display) with Ussher, Jones and, where available, CFAH-1 Table 1 dates for sorting. Jordan treats the judgeships as partly overlapping regional sequences (North / Centre / South) fitted to the 480 years of 1 Kgs 6:1 and the 300 years of Judg 11:26.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (F. N. Jones): 1218 BC (no higher-tier year available). Jordan (secondary display) never sets the sort.

chronologies.citation: Jones, Chart No. 4 "Judges to the First 3 Kings" (© 1993 Floyd Jones; chart text revised "As of 2007"), timeline band

chronologies.date: 2769d AM, 1235 BC (Abimelech made king with the Shechemites' help)
chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Fourth Age §358 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
chronologies.note: §357 (2768d AM, 1236 BC): Gideon dies; Abimelech kills his brothers. §359 (2771d AM, 1233 BC): after three years Gaal's conspiracy and Abimelech's death.

chronologies.citation: Jordan, From Creation to Solomon (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2, Biblical Horizons, Oct. 2001), ch. 11 "The Era of the Judges and the Reign of Saul", p. 52
chronologies.note: 2001 revision. Jordan's 1991 list (BC 3:8) has an earlier year; see the second Jordan entry.

chronologies.date: "2787 - Death of Gideon, beginning of Abimelech's 3-year oppressive reign (Jud. 9:22)."
chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Chronology and Kings (II)," Biblical Chronology 3:8 (August 1991), section "The Judges", summary list
chronologies.note: 1991 scheme, superseded by Jordan himself in 2001 (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2 dates the whole judges sequence 26 years later because he there ends the 300 years of Judg 11:26 when Ammon took the villages, AM 2860, not at Jephthah's victory). BC 5:2: "Gideon died in 2787, and his evil son Abimelech became Israel's first king. His death ... came in 2790, a sabbath year."

chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 8, chart "Year of the World: From the Judges to King Saul (Chronology from James Jordan)"
chronologies.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 2813.
